description:
We’re a team exploring NASA Earth data to detect important environmental trends and understand how our planet is changing over time.

We’ll use Python, Data Processing, Time Series, Machine Learning, NLP, and interactive visualizations to turn complex data into simple, useful insights.
summary:
*The Warming World* explores how climate change is transforming polar environments and creating wider environmental risks. We developed a data-driven analysis using NASA/NSIDC satellite observations of Arctic and Antarctic sea ice from 1990 to 2026. Through data cleaning, exploratory analysis, statistical trend testing, and time-series forecasting, the project investigates historical sea-ice changes and explores possible trends through 2050.

Beyond measuring ice loss, the project connects these changes to vulnerable polar wildlife, including polar bears and emperor penguins, and examines the wider implications for coastal communities and historical monuments. It also explores potential sea-level-rise scenarios and coastal exposure, while distinguishing measured satellite data from external assumptions.

By combining scientific data, visual storytelling, and future projections, *The Warming World* aims to make the impacts of climate change easier to understand and highlight the importance of reducing emissions, protecting ecosystems, and preparing vulnerable coastal regions for the future.
details:
The Warming World: Climate Trends Analysis and Future Forecasting

The Warming World is a data-driven climate analysis project that investigates historical climate patterns, identifies long-term environmental trends, and forecasts potential future changes using NASA Earth observation data.

The project focuses on analyzing key climate variables, including temperature, specific humidity, and precipitation, alongside additional polar sea ice analysis. It uses historical monthly observations to understand seasonal patterns, long-term variations, and relationships between different climate indicators.

Our methodology combines Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), statistical analysis, time-series decomposition, stationarity testing, and SARIMA forecasting. We use these techniques to identify historical trends and generate future projections, including long-term forecasts extending to 2050.

The project provides interactive visual insights through time-series plots, seasonal comparisons, trend analysis, and forecast uncertainty visualizations. These results help make complex climate data easier to understand and communicate.

The main benefit of this project is transforming large-scale Earth observation data into meaningful information that can support climate awareness, environmental research, and evidence-based decision-making.

What makes our approach creative is combining multiple climate indicators with statistical forecasting and long-term trend analysis in a unified workflow. Instead of examining individual observations in isolation, the project connects historical patterns with potential future climate behavior.

Technologies Used:

  • Python
  • Pandas and NumPy
  • Matplotlib and Seaborn
  • Statsmodels (SARIMA and time-series analysis)
  • Jupyter Notebook
  • NASA Earthdata and Giovanni

The project aims to demonstrate how accessible satellite and climate datasets, combined with data science techniques, can help us better understand our changing planet.
